related_resources.reason: Index confirms lectures 6 (Turing machines), 7 (decidability), 8 (undecidability), and 9 (mapping reducibility and Rice theorem). Slides credited to Prof. Nancy Lynch; index rather than linked PDFs read.
P, NP, reductions, complexity categories; lecture summary and educational resource.
Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 74(2), 358–366; bibliography/DOI corroborated; source of named theorem, not falsely presented as fully read.
Sections 1 and 2 describe historical calculi, universality, halting undecidability, complexity.
Sections 2.3 and 2.4.1–2.4.3: universality, diagonal and Turing original circle-free versus contemporary halting formulation; 2025 revision verified.
Course reference indexes recognizer, decider, complement, and co-recognizable terminology; tool-visible search excerpts, not independent proof of the theorem.

claim_evidence.anchor: If problem A reduces to problem B, then a solution to B provides a solution to A.
claim_evidence.source_locator: SEP Turing Machines §2.4 and Computability and Complexity §4.1, reduction direction.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: SEP Turing Machines §2.4 and Computability and Complexity §4.1, reduction direction.

claim_evidence.anchor: The impossible task must reduce into the task whose impossibility we wish to establish.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Contrapositive of decider-transfer theorem in companion.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Contrapositive of decider-transfer theorem in companion.

claim_evidence.anchor: The transformation must itself be computable.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Definition of many-one/mapping reduction A ≤m B, MIT 6.045J lecture 9 index.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Definition of many-one/mapping reduction A ≤m B, MIT 6.045J lecture 9 index.

claim_evidence.anchor: And it must preserve both answers: yes turns into yes, and no turns into no.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Biconditional x∈A iff f(x)∈B, not only positive preservation.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Biconditional x∈A iff f(x)∈B, not only positive preservation.

claim_evidence.anchor: Therefore if A is undecidable and A reduces to B, B must be undecidable too.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Proof in narration using composition with target decider.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Proof in narration using composition with target decider.

claim_evidence.anchor: If B has a recognizer and A maps to B, compute f of x and run B's recognizer.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Preservation of recognizability under total computable mapping reductions.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Preservation of recognizability under total computable mapping reductions.

claim_evidence.anchor: A rejecting machine halts without accepting, and a looping machine does neither.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Stanford CS103 recognizer/decider terminology and machine acceptance.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Stanford CS103 recognizer/decider terminology and machine acceptance.

claim_evidence.anchor: the halting problem maps to the acceptance problem.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Construction: N accepts iff original M halts on fixed w. HALT ≤m A_TM.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Construction: N accepts iff original M halts on fixed w. HALT ≤m A_TM.

claim_evidence.anchor: We do not run M to completion while constructing N
claim_evidence.source_locator: Totality of source-to-source compilation; input/w are embedded as constants in generated N.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Totality of source-to-source compilation; input/w are embedded as constants in generated N.

claim_evidence.anchor: Since halting is not decidable, acceptance is not decidable either.
claim_evidence.source_locator: HALT ≤m A_TM and contrapositive of transfer theorem.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. HALT ≤m A_TM and contrapositive of transfer theorem.

claim_evidence.anchor: So the acceptance problem reduces to the halting problem.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Construction: rejecting outcome becomes loop, acceptance becomes halt; A_TM ≤m HALT.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Construction: rejecting outcome becomes loop, acceptance becomes halt; A_TM ≤m HALT.

claim_evidence.anchor: These questions are not identical.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Rejecting halt belongs to HALT but not A_TM; semantic distinction.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Rejecting halt belongs to HALT but not A_TM; semantic distinction.

claim_evidence.anchor: In fact, it is undecidable.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Constructive A_TM ≤m NONEMPTY_TM in succeeding paragraphs; Rice historical author reference.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Constructive A_TM ≤m NONEMPTY_TM in succeeding paragraphs; Rice historical author reference.

claim_evidence.anchor: the accepted language of N is the entire input universe in the yes case and the empty set in the no case.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Two-case calculation L(N)=Σ* if M(w) accepts else ∅.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Two-case calculation L(N)=Σ* if M(w) accepts else ∅.

claim_evidence.anchor: The transformation from M and w to N is algorithmic
claim_evidence.source_locator: Code generator outputs finite N description; does not decide M(w) while generating.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Code generator outputs finite N description; does not decide M(w) while generating.

claim_evidence.anchor: It therefore directly reduces acceptance to nonemptiness, not to emptiness.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Direction and membership orientation audited; A_TM ≤m NONEMPTY_TM, not E_TM.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Direction and membership orientation audited; A_TM ≤m NONEMPTY_TM, not E_TM.

claim_evidence.anchor: A reduction is a construction with a proof of behavior, not a solver hidden inside a compiler.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Total mapping construction may not run potentially divergent M(w) during translation.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Total mapping construction may not run potentially divergent M(w) during translation.

claim_evidence.anchor: This is the familiar language-property formulation of *Rice's theorem*
claim_evidence.source_locator: Rice 1953 original publication metadata; MIT 6.045J lecture 9 title explicitly Rice theorem.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Rice 1953 original publication metadata; MIT 6.045J lecture 9 title explicitly Rice theorem.

claim_evidence.anchor: It applies to recognized languages, not to the syntax of one implementation.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Rice property extensional on recognized language L(M).
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Rice property extensional on recognized language L(M).

claim_evidence.anchor: Call the property P.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Setup for original full proof in narration and mathematical companion.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Setup for original full proof in narration and mathematical companion.

claim_evidence.anchor: First suppose the empty language does not have P.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Case split of theorem P(∅) false/true.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Case split of theorem P(∅) false/true.

claim_evidence.anchor: If M accepts w, the initial simulation eventually finishes in acceptance, after which N behaves like T on each x.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Constructed N recognizes L(T) on yes case; proof obligation explicit.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Constructed N recognizes L(T) on yes case; proof obligation explicit.

claim_evidence.anchor: N recognizes the empty language, which does not have P.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Constructed N recognizes ∅ if source M(w) does not accept.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Constructed N recognizes ∅ if source M(w) does not accept.

claim_evidence.anchor: If P had a decider, we could swap yes and no to decide its complement.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Second case P(∅) true, apply previous argument to ¬P.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Second case P(∅) true, apply previous argument to ¬P.

claim_evidence.anchor: Whether a machine halts on every input is a property of its execution behavior
claim_evidence.source_locator: Rice applies only to accepted-language-extensional properties, unlike totality.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Rice applies only to accepted-language-extensional properties, unlike totality.

claim_evidence.anchor: Both recognize the empty language: neither accepts any string.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Machine rejecting all vs looping all, witness totality not language property.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Machine rejecting all vs looping all, witness totality not language property.

claim_evidence.anchor: whether the accepted language is regular *is* a language property.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Nontrivial extensional property; DFA languages recognizable; 0^n1^n recognizable nonregular, discussed in companion.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Nontrivial extensional property; DFA languages recognizable; 0^n1^n recognizable nonregular, discussed in companion.

claim_evidence.anchor: mapping reductions only need to be computable; they need not be efficient in the sense of polynomial running time.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Computability and Complexity §4.1 distinguishes complexity reduction bounds from computability.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Computability and Complexity §4.1 distinguishes complexity reduction bounds from computability.

claim_evidence.anchor: the reduction itself must obey an explicit resource bound, usually polynomial time.
claim_evidence.source_locator: SEP §4.1 and MIT 6.006 complexity lecture on polynomial reductions.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: SEP §4.1 and MIT 6.006 complexity lecture on polynomial reductions.

claim_evidence.anchor: Only then take the contrapositive: a decider for the target would decide the source
claim_evidence.source_locator: Explicit proof checklist and contrapositive theorem.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Explicit proof checklist and contrapositive theorem.
